newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan Hutus say 500,000 refugees face death.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan Hutus say 500,000 refugees face death.

text.p: A lobby group for Rwandan Hutus said on Tuesday half-a-million refugees in Zaire had received no food or water for 15 days and it accused the international community of failing them.

"Some 500,000 refugees in South Kivu have been without food, water or medicine for 15 days. Another 700,000 refugees in North Kivu, around Goma, are facing the same fate," said the Rally for the Return of Refugees and Democracy in Rwanda (RDR).
A two-week-old Tutsi rebel offensive in eastern Zaire hit towns in South Kivu province first, before moving against North Kivu, which aid workers evacuated last Saturday.

Information on the refugees' plight is scarce since the fighting has effectively cut them off from the outside world. France and Spain on Monday called for a U.N.-sanctioned military force to go into Zaire to ensure the refugees can get food.

The Europe-based RDR said in a statement: "While in Bosnia, Liberia, Iraq, Somalia, just to mention a few, the international community promptly responded to similar tragedies, by creating safe zones for refugees, the plight of those Hutu refugees does not seem to move the champions of human rights."
The group said since early October attacks on Zaire refugee camps by Rwandan and Burundian troops had left thousands dead.
"The rest are facing sure death by starvation, exhaustion and lack of medicine," it said.

Rwanda and Burundi deny their forces have attacked refugee camps in Zaire. Correspondents have seen Rwandan forces fighting in the Zairean city of Goma, but it has not been possible for reporters to reach the refugee camps.

The RDR said Rwanda and its allies aimed to cut off all supply routes into the refugee camps by capturing the airports of Butembo, Bunia and Kisangani in eastern Zaire. It said the airports of Goma and Bukavu were already out of use.
The Rwandan refugees in Zaire fled their homeland in 1994 fearing reprisals for the Hutu genocide up to one million Tutsis and other victims. Both Rwanda and Burundi now have Tutsi-led governments.
In its 12-page statement, the RDR accused the Rwandan army and Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels of a series of atrocities at refugee camps in Zaire over the past few weeks.
It said Rwandan soldiers and Banyamulenge attacked the camps of Runingo in Uvira on the northern shore of Lake Tanganyika in early October and killed refugees who fled.
"Those whose legs could not carry them farther were summarily executed and their bodies thrown into Lake Tanganyika," it said.
